themes.label: Energy system paywall backlash
themes.summary: Most reviews in this cluster praise Duolingo as fun, simple, and effective, so the low 2.60 average is driven by a subset of users. Those critics say a newer energy bar drains even after perfect lessons, limits free practice, and pushes users toward Super, with ads and reshuffled or repeated lessons adding to the frustration. Several reviewers say they are considering leaving or deleting the app.
themes.recommendation: Pull energy depletion, session drop-off, and Super conversion data by app version (v7.90 onward) and by platform, then test a variant that does not deduct energy for perfect lessons or that raises the free daily allowance, and track review sentiment for the energy topic.

themes.label: Energy system limits lessons
themes.summary: Many users say the energy or hearts system now caps how many lessons they can finish per day, often forcing them to watch ads or pay for Super even when answering correctly. Several describe the app as having become heavily monetized and gamified, with some calling the energy mechanic a dark pattern. The complaints appear across both Android and iOS and in recent app versions, with a few long-time users saying they are considering cancelling.
themes.recommendation: Pull energy consumption logs and funnel data for Android and iOS on recent versions (v6.9x and v7.x) to measure how many correct answers still cost energy, then test a version where correct answers in completed lessons do not drain energy or where the daily cap is raised for free users.

themes.label: Aggressive monetization, ads, and paywalls
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the free experience has become unusable, with energy or heart limits that cut lessons short, frequent ads (including ads for Super), and XP loss that pushes them toward subscriptions. Many describe the paywall as predatory, and several say they feel punished for not paying. Some also feel the app's learning value has declined as monetization has increased.
themes.recommendation: Audit the free-tier energy, heart, and ad frequency per session against the current subscription funnel, and run an A/B test that reduces ads and energy restrictions for free users to measure retention and rating impact.

themes.label: Backlash against AI-first layoffs
themes.summary: Users are angry that Duolingo announced an AI-first strategy and reportedly replaced human workers, especially translators and staff, with AI. Many say they are deleting the app or cancelling subscriptions in protest, and some cite AI-generated lesson content, voices, and explanations that feel inaccurate or lifeless. The complaints appear across both iOS and Android, clustered around app versions from spring 2025 onward.
themes.recommendation: Have leadership and the communications team publish a clear statement on how AI is used in content creation and which roles changed, then track churn and uninstall rates for the weeks following it to measure how much this backlash is costing retention.

themes.label: Gamification and monetization pressure backlash
themes.summary: Long-time users say recent updates added hearts or energy limits, a timer, streak guilt notifications, aggressive ads, and paywalled practice, making lessons feel stressful and pay-to-progress. Many compare the current app unfavorably to earlier versions and say they are uninstalling or switching to other apps, including users with very long streaks. Several also mention AI-driven changes and the icon's emotional tone as contributing to the sense that the core learning experience has been diluted.
themes.recommendation: Pull a cohort analysis of churn and uninstall rates before and after the heart-to-energy and timer changes, segmented by free versus paid users, and test a version that restores practice-based heart recovery and reduces streak-related push notification frequency.

themes.label: Course updates add unlearned words
themes.summary: Users report that recent course and learning path updates reordered lessons and inserted vocabulary they never studied, often into units they had already completed, which leaves them lost and sometimes resets their progress or streaks. Several say the changes apply across both iOS and Android and across multiple courses, including Japanese and French, and some say completed lessons no longer count or that support has not responded.
themes.recommendation: Audit the course update pipeline to confirm that newly added vocabulary is gated behind the lessons that teach it, and ensure completed-unit status and streaks are preserved when paths are reordered; ship a rollback or 'revert to previous path' option and track support response times for these reports.

themes.label: Hearts replaced by energy system
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android are angry that the hearts mechanic, and later the energy meter that replaced it, now caps how many lessons they can do, with many saying energy drains even on correct answers. Several also say practice no longer refills hearts unless they're at zero, and they read the change as a push to upsell premium subscriptions.
themes.recommendation: Pull session data for energy depletion since the energy rollout (v7.84 onward) and compare lessons completed per session and drop-off points against the old hearts system, then test whether charging energy only for incorrect answers or restoring practice-to-earn hearts keeps engagement without hurting conversion.

themes.label: Energy system limits lessons
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the energy system that replaced hearts drains too fast, so they can finish only one to three lessons before being blocked, even when answering correctly. Many feel the change pushes them toward ads or paid subscriptions, and several say they have stopped learning or uninstalled as a result. Some also report energy refills not registering and streaks failing to update after lessons.
themes.recommendation: Pull energy consumption and refill logs for lessons from the last two app versions (v6.85 to v7.134) to compare energy spent per correct answer against the old heart model, and test a change so correct answers no longer deduct energy or the per-lesson cost is reduced, with a separate bug ticket for missing energy rewards and streak updates.

Duolingo claims to make English testing accessible to people “anywhere in the world,” yet it is now denying Iranian students access to the Duolingo English Test simply because of where they are from or because they have an Iranian-issued ID. I have the paid version of the app. Overall I find it helpful (as a beginner), but there are a few issues with it. There are quite a few explanations for the grammar that seem to be incorrect (nominative vs dative articles in particular for German). They often give incorrect hints. They play ads constantly between lessons which can cost you a minute or more of your bonus time. They make you watch ads for super that you cannot mute. They often make words like 'di' 'ti' and 'ci' sound the same which is really frustrating and can cost you if you make a mistake. All in all I recommend going and finding a better translation app.

Hello! I’ve been using Duo for several years now, and it saddens me to see this app getting worse and worse. And while free users are being pushed more and more aggressively to buy paid lessons, Duo is also cheating those who actually pay for classes. I won’t even get into the terrible interface, the awful avatars, the app icon with a snotty or idiotic face (after all, a drooling Duo is the height of silliness), or the crude and pointless attempt to mimic social media. I’ll say just one thing: I’m getting ripped off. Duo steals points, Duo steals the number of weeks spent in the League, and Duo steals completed lessons (assignments that are tallied at the beginning of each month). The microphone might not work and might not “hear” your answer. I’m tired of seeing random bots in my feed. One minute they’re competing in the weekly rankings and racking up an unrealistic number of points (scores). The next minute, these bots have thousands or tens of thousands of likes under their posts. I’m tired of looking at a cheap interface that looks like something out of a kids’ adventure game. I’m tired of reading silly motivational messages like “you need to broaden your horizons,” “why do you need so many points?,” “conduct experiments,” and so on. Who is all this nonsense aimed at? I’m tired of realizing over and over again that Duo is just taking your money and… that’s it. The app stopped being educational a long time ago. It’s turned into a cheap (not in a monetary sense, but in terms of the effort put in) attempt to become a social network. You often write that millions of users use your app. You’d be better off counting how many users have left because of these prompts and updates.

reviews.t: Each update is unfortunately worse than the last
reviews.x: I’ve been at this now for nearly 2 years. Each update scrambles your lessons and sets you back because you have to relearn where you are in their curriculum. You’ll often get new words you’ve never learned, or get lessons that you’ve already done. There’s no meaningful “improvement” with these adjustments, just changes. It derails your learning until you can sort it out, which can sometimes take days or weeks depending on how much time you have to work through the lessons and how quickly you progress. The latest update has me stuck on a lesson that just repeats over and over. Even going all the way to the beginning and reviewing the very first lesson hasn’t helped. I’m forever stuck reviewing words like “a” “and” and “coffee” along with phrases like “with sugar”. I’ll occasionally get a completely random review lesson of something I had never learned. Progressing is out of the question as it offers words and phrases I’ve never seen, with nothing to build on. Support is unfortunately non existent as Duolingo has gone hard toward AI, and I’m not sure the feedback function even does anything. Not that it’s really meant as a support tool anyways. I’m holding on hoping that the next update fixes my issues, but at this stage I can’t reasonably recommend Duolingo to anyone. It’s a shame as it was a great tool to get me to return to a small lesson daily when I started learning, something that was very helpful in the early stages of trying to pick up a new language.

The app is more focused on getting ur cash on every step of the way instead of actually be a tool to learn. At the time of the review. The best u can do is learn 2 lessons before the energy runs out and the app start begging u for money.

The hearts system was much better, it allowed you to continue learning for free if you weren’t making mistakes. Now with the energy system, I can barely do 2 lessons, and if I make mistakes, then I probably can’t even do 2 lessons. This app sold out and is a complete joke now
It’s good and all but I need to watch ads all the time, after each lesson, an ad about buying max. Wanna practice more? Ad. It’s ANNOYING.

reviews.t: The battery is very annoying and there is too many ads.
reviews.x: it used to be so easy to learn and it still is but it’s full of ads. The battery thing is also very annoying.

After every level you get an advertisement and a bunch of repetitive popups. Their energy system is horrible, you are basically forced to only do one or two levels a day, forcing you to spend your gems to refill your energy or purchase their subscription that they always advertise after every level. Duolingo was a much better app a couple years ago but now it feels almost unfamiliar and soulless.
I hate the adds like it comes up every single time and the energy is just sad plus Duolingo getting mad as a don’t play I don’t agree with this one star

at first i really love this app. it's cool i can learn a lot of languages, i can even learn math & music BUT the super/max ads this app gives everytime i finished learning is too much seriously. it's so annoying, give it but not everytime i finished. okay i know the super thing is cool like we can even do training, but NOT ALL ppl have it, so the ads is definitely too much. better if this ads thing is fixed to less ads, i hope u understand the ppl that don't have this super/max pack.

The new update they put instead of lives they switched it to energy which is total bs can’t even learn a single lesson without my energy running out so fast, yall are really that money hungry?? Useless app… Deleted.

Don’t expect to learn anything from this app. They put way more effort into monetization and nagging the user than actually teaching anything. This app takes gamification to the extreme to the point where using it is no longer fun or educational.

Do learn Spanish here. Do not learn Korean here. Korean starts out great. You'll get a good tiny foundation, but section 2 tanks in quality. It no longer repeats vocabulary at you. You are expected to suddenly know new vocabulary you weren't taught which is worked around by tapping, but it feels messy. You're more worried about if you're reading it and pronouncing it right, if its new vocab or you just got vowels mixed up than what the focus is on. i.e. sentence structure, positive/negative

reviews.t: They got rid of the hearts
reviews.x: This is such a stupid update. I loved using the hearts because then at least you had more time before you completely ran out. But they had to switch it to this stupid energy thing now and it makes you run out of energy during each question which is so stupid. Bring back the hearts!!

reviews.t: Spend more time watching ads than learning
reviews.x: Used to be excellent, now the energy update made it so you just have to watch more ads than lessons. Used to be after a lesson there would be an ad, now after every lesson you have to basically watch 3 ads if you want keep doing lessons.

Using the energy sucks… I used to be able to do so many lessons until I made 5 mistakes. Now I can only do 2-3 lessons before my energy depletes. The cost of gems for energy is too high, just for it to be used quickly. It only lets me watch about 5 ads for extra energy and then the option to watch ads isn’t even there anymore. The hearts were a way better system. Please bring them back.

Title: My Streak Deserves Better 😭🔥 Dear Duolingo Team, I love your app like, actually love it. I’ve been protecting my streak harder than I protect my snacks from my siblings. But today… tragedy struck. I ran out of Energy. I had barely any Gems. And suddenly I’m staring at two options: 1. Lose my beautiful, loyal, hard-earned streak, or 2. Pay for Super Duolingo, which my wallet screamed at immediately. Listen, I totally get that apps need money to run. But please… why must my streak suffer for my financial situation? 😭 My streak didn’t do anything wrong. My streak deserves to live. It would be amazing if you could: • Let users buy Energy for fewer Gems, or • Give a small amount of Energy daily, or • Let streaks be protected without having to pay. I promise I’m trying to learn Duo please don’t make me choose between knowledge and bankruptcy. Sincerely, A loyal learner who is dramatically guarding their streak with their life 🫡🦉🔥
This app uses an energy system (like in many mobile game) to limit the amount of lessons you can do in a day. Not practical.

reviews.t: Pick another app if you actually want to learn
reviews.x: Beyond the fact that the translations are not perfect, and sometimes useless. The update from hearts to a timer has made this app entirely unusable for free members. The push notifications every 5 minutes while I’m doing other things on my phone are unbearable. Not to mention you give me 3-5 minutes of play time until I can’t continue because of the timer. They have shamelessly ruined this app in the past year. Deleted and won’t be back.

EDIT: Removing 2 stars from my previous review. The app used to have hearts that remained as long as you got everything correct, now it's got this stupid energy system that runs out regardless of how much you get right. That's not rewarding, it's frustrating. You know what else is frustrating? When I say EXACTLY what the app wants me to say it fails to hear me correctly and I get the answer wrong. Why do I only get 3 attempts? I should be able to speak until I get it right on speaking exercises.

every time I think this game couldn't get any worse, it does. the new energy thing is stupid. I don't want to buy your stupid premium. if you gave me an option just to get rid of ads I would do it. but I like the fact that there's a risk of losing and having unlimited energy takes that away. you guys are really starting to suck.

Duolingo has so many mistakes in the app that is infuriating, they show you the right answer but you the word is not even there,also when the work makes a sound but is the wrong spelling,when you are learning a language like Japanese everything matter,not just right or wrong,if you are trying to get to the next level on any language I recommend to get a real person that can actually explain. Duolingo will only give you the illusion that you are learning a new language

Been using this app basically since it was started, its gone downhill so bad. I dont mind paying, but its gotten more expensive for less. They used to let you use gems to buy different thing (duo costumes, different little lessons like a romantic sayings lesson, you used to be able to buy boosts)now you cant do any of that. Its lost its charm, and i swearbi get the same lessons in a row.Now they have energy instead of lives, so it doesnt matter if you make a mistake, you lose energy after a move

I used to like it. This new "energy" system SUCKS. You can't do nearly as many lessons as under the hearts method. You just run out and there's no way to re-up... other than to pay. They really screwed up the experience with this. The enshitification of everything continues.

reviews.t: The new ‘energy’ thing is ruining everything 🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬
reviews.x: Before everything was fantastic until they updated the ‘energy’ thing. Sometimes, even I got everything correct I can’t even finish 2 units. 😡YOU LOSE ENERGY EVEN YOU ARE CORRECT😡. The whole thing is terrible and friends of mine deleted this app because of this. This is not the best app to learn a foreign language anymore, check other apps before you come back

I have rolled with all the changes in this app for three years. I dislike that I get "docked" energy points for giving correct answers. The "extra credit" I receive when I make five correct answers in a row are just not enough. I've completed a lesson a few times while on my last energy and lost progress. It's a real downer when you were counting on that for your badge before midnight.
Switching to this “energy” system that you lose energy even with a right answer has completely ruined the experience.

The new energy mechanic is devastatingly awful, and it has immediately transformed a good app into something many people will abandon and forget. It's bound to alienate users via some classic, cynical greed. It's making the app unenjoyable and unusable. No one will bother with Duolingo if they can't finish their lessons or learn a single thing in the ad version. At least the heart system was based on performance. It was fair. Now, it's just a shameless paywall.

The new energy system makes the free membership pretty much impossible to use. Even if you're perfect, you can only get about 3 lessons done. I went from being able to do 6-8 lessons to barely 3. This ruins the app's purpose to teach languages unless you can afford the paid version, which completely goes against the app's original purpose. It's clear that the company has shifted their focus from teaching language to doing whatever they have to to make money, even when it ruins their app.

It used to be great to include some foreign words and expressions into the real life context. Also, it somehow helped overcome a new language barrier due to speaking practice. But they introduced Energy instead of hearts and it sucks - I can't concentrate on studying any more and should constantly watch ads. I'm thinking about looking for alternatives. Also, it doesn't explain grammar properly and there's no European Spanish.

This app used to be a great way to learn a language. You learn at your own pace-as much or as little as you like. Not anymore. The hearts system they used was perfectly fine but they changed it to the energy system-21 pieces of energy. Answer a question,1 piece gone,claim xp at the end of a round another piece gone. Some rounds have 17 questions-21 energy doesn't go far. They give you 2 & 3 for 5 & 10 streaks and 5 for a perfect round. Getting 10 back for 17 qs plus xp claim,18 total-ridiculous

I like the app. I have learned a lot. The grammar rules for languages need to be clear. Sometimes I don't understand the sentences that I'm putting together. Also, some translations don't match up with the words in the word bank. For example, "A Ana treina aqui" is supposed to be "Ana trains here" in English. The words that I had to choose from made the sentence "Ana is training here". Also, random new words were thrown in at the end of a few units. I'm not feeling Duo wearing make-up either.

This app has really declined over the years. Aside from becoming overrun with ads in an attempt to make you spend money, they now just recycle the same handful of phrases among units. This means you're not actually learning the principles of the language and how to apply them, but rather just memorizing sentences.

For a while there have been bugs in the app that the 'daily refresh' of the music lessons would not be matched up with the songs actual names. Another bug is that sometimes you would get a reward but it wouldn't actually show up and you didn't actually get it. Another thing that bothers me is the Duolingo ad that has someone sitting in the restroom, and a few other ads. They don't seem appropriate, as children use this app too. Otherwise besides these things the app teaches lessons pretty well.

This app used to be great for learning, however it has gone downhill with every update. Not only does it take up a huge amount of space but it has essentially become unusable with the “energy” level instead of hearts, my kid uses the kid version and says “why is it punishing me for getting the right answers?” I have to agree. Get back to what it used to be, otherwise people shouldn’t even bother installing this one.

reviews.t: Duolingo please bring back the hearts!
reviews.x: This app used to be good until they changed from hearts to a battery, now I can barely do ONE lesson

I was always on the fence if I wanted to keep doing this game. While I was learning words and general sentence structure, I never felt confident actually speaking Spanish. now they changed the game. before you lost hearts if you get an answer wrong. now instead of hearts,energy which can be lost just for answering a question, you can run out of energy mid game even when answering correctly, causing you to pay in jewels to keep playing or exit out. this seems like a good time to find another app.

I see how everyone thought the hearts were a bad choice. I was fine with it because you could keep going if you didn’t make mistakes. Now theres “energy” a really stupid system where you LOSE energy if you answer correctly and lose EVEN MORE energy if you make mistakes… you could answer everything right and eventually you will lose all your energy and will have to wait for it to refill. Awful system, I don’t recommend. This used to be a good app

Overall not bad, but the grammar can be a bit fussy at times, and insists on everything being 100% literary correct, which is not how humans talk. I would also appreciate if for verb conjugation we got tables so we can read them all, instead of being drip-fed one at a time. Plus, lately there's been an issue with the app icon on Android. As a Super Duolingo user, I cannot change it, and it's stuck on Duolingo crying, for some reason. Even if I haven't lost my streak even one time. Why is that?

My comments on the Lilly phone calls keeps saying something different from what I'm actually saying. It's extremely frustrating and is holding me back from engaging in an actual conversation. I wish they explained the usage of the words better. All of a sudden the usage of the words changes to a different spelling of the word and I don't know why. I seem to be googling the differences between words more than using your app. And google is free.
I dont normally go out of my way to write a review but the new energy system is terrible. Such a disappointment

Charge System is broken. Answering all correctly cant even reward you enough to continue to the next 3 lessons on a full energy bar. The heart system was way better in terms of learning, this new system results into more time watching ads and less time actually learning something. It is also buggy when rewarding energy, when you have 1 energy left, even when the question results for an energy bonus, it doesn’t add to the energy bar.

reviews.t: I really liked it but not anymore
reviews.x: After the new update that caused you to only do a few practices before you run out of energy where as you used to be able to practice as much as you wanted to unless you didn’t make a mistake. Awful

energy system is terrible. i ran out after three perfect lessons and am forced to stop my lessons or pay. bad.

REMOVE ENERGY!! The energy does not help users who have mistakes as advertised, it just limits how many lessons one can take regardless of performance. Even if you get perfect lessons you are still only able to do 2 or 3 lessons per day, and if your lessons aren't perfect you are only able to do 1 or maybe 2 per day. Besides that, ever since it adopted an AI model, there have been cases of inaccurate or straight up wrong translations.

reviews.t: Energy is a terrible, greedy change
reviews.x: Duolingo switched from hearts to energy and it is absolutely terrible now. Before, with hearts, you could practice as much as you wanted as long as you weren’t making mistakes. Now with energy, every step of a lesson uses energy even when answering correctly. Now you can barely complete two to three lessons without running out, even when answering everything right. This is such an awful change that is clearly motivated by greed. They are punishing people who aren’t on super (paid subscription) but not actively letting them learn anymore. It’s actually pathetic.
This energy system practically makes the app unusable, you can barely get through 3 lessons before you run out of energy, even if you answer everything correct!

750 days, I was learning and managed to make it through their updates that restarted my lessons, my progress, and entire courses, but the newest energy system shows me that their bottom line and money is more important than teaching. Sayonara Duolingo. It was fun.

reviews.t: Energy update makes this a terrible app.
reviews.x: I used to love duolingo but now with this new update it has become nearly useless without a paid subscription. If you do a perfect lesson you still lose energy. reviews.t: Energy Instead of Hearts Is A Wrong Move
reviews.x: I feel like the time to ditch Duolingo is coming inevitably closer. In pursuit of revenue, the move from hearts, which by the end of a tenth lesson (so to speak) could still be five out of five if you don't make mistakes, to an energy bar, which ”discharges” no matter the mistakes, is a wrong one. I understand the need for monetization (which I occasionally pay for diamonds, too to support the app developers), but not at this expense. If this is not turned to the previous mode with hearts, Duo the owl will lose yet another member in a matter of seconds

the heart system was already garbage enough and now what is this energy system. like it takes energy away from SIMPLY ANSWERING A QUESTION. im actually about to stop learning a language. maybe the creators of duolingo knows its a useless app and tries to make it worse so people wont use it.

I loved the app before the switch the heart system to the battery system that makes no sense. Can't even do three lessons in a day it is ridiculous. Will gladly switch to another learning app

The recent change from hearts to battery ruins the entire experience sadly. Limits the actual learning regardless of how well you’re doing to maybe a few lessons per day which isn’t at all helpful for learning a language. Please change back to the previous hearts system. It wasn’t perfect but at least it was better than this new garbage system.

I have a 6+ year old streak in this app and have seen many changes throughout the years. But this one stops you from doing more lessons compared to the hearts. I hope they listen to their users and change it back soon.

They changed the heart system (already annoying, but fine) for batteries/charge that loses value every time you learn! You have to use 400+ “gems” to refill in the middle of a lesson, subscribe to their premium service, or you have to quit midway through. Absolutely horrible design with zero thought for people actually interested in learning. There are so many ads on this app that there is no way they need to push their subscription service to this extent. I thought this was a language learning app, but it’s just a desperate attempt to get people subscribed to a $30 monthly service…

reviews.t: Somewhat okay for language, terrible for free users!
reviews.x: I deleted the app a few months ago due to the replacement of employees by AI, but couldn’t find another “free” avenue for very basic German, so I decided I’d give it a go again. MISTAKE! This new energy system is one of the most idiotic things I have seen implemented in a while. Punishing you for learning? Seriously? At least with the hearts, you could go as long as you wanted, given you made no mistakes. But now? I cannot even finish 4 lessons and I am already out of energy. I used to blast through because I could grasp the courses easily, but that is no longer an option. Now I have to wait before I can even think about doing another lesson! I mean, how is that fair? The goal of this app is to make language learning more accessible, isn’t it? Apparently they forgot that! I’m genuinely disappointed by that absolute nonsense of a system and I hope by everything under the sun that it disintegrates like a surface when you pour a highly corrosive compound on it. I HATE IT. ☺️☺️

Until the latest update, it was possible to learn without a subscription. Now it’s only possible to do 2 lessons a day without watching at least 4 ads per level to get enough “health” to get through it, even without any mistakes. If you do t want people to play without a subscription, just be honest about it!

The implementation of the hearts years ago, giving you the rights to make 5 mistakes, have slowed me a lot in my progression making me stop using the app. But I decided to give it another try to learn another language. However they now decided to replace the hearts by an energy bar, with which I can’t practice more than 5 minutes. I usually don’t make much mistakes which allows me to practice as much as I want, but now, with every answer, good or bad, you loose one energy point and you have a total of 25 only. I would really appreciate if it goes back to the hearts instead of the energy bar, otherwise I will use another app.

reviews.t: New free option is worse, you can not only do one lesson per day
reviews.x: The old free option gave you five hearts (five opportunities to fail), but now it’s an energy score that depletes whether you’re right or wrong, so it limits you to one lesson per day. It may be good with the paid version, but not worth it for the free version
they fired almost all their staff to use cheap AI that pollutes the word.. plus you have to watch too many ads and are locked out of the additional features

reviews.t: The worst update in human history

What kind of twisted individual thought it would be a good idea to make you lose lives for getting the answer correct. This app is no longer about learning new languages , it’s about watching ads and buying gems. You have drifted so far from the light duo. 🦜🪦

First the hearts and now energy? It is too hard to learn because if you make mistakes it will prevent you from doing lessons. Mistakes are natural and you are supposed to learn from them not be punished. And if you thought the hearts were bad, now there is energy which limits how much you can do even if you get everything right. Also there is no way this app is 5 stars because If you scroll through all the reviews they are all 2 or less. I am deleting this app because they are too greedy.

I really like the app. It's a great way to learn languages. But, PLEASE remove the Video Call Max upgrade as a main button. I already pay for the Super and have zero interest in spending the ridiculously high price for Max. I want the Practice Hub back as the default button. I was not happy about that Max stuff being pushed in my line of sight, but now I'm irritated that I need to select ellipses button to get to Practice Hub. Max should be there for those buying it. I am not going to.

The new recharge thing is pretty irritating. On many occasions I almost finish a lesson only to have run out of battery. It’s even worse than the hearts. I feel even more pressure to make less mistakes. It makes me less motivated to learn, on top of tolerating the monetization.

Who came up with this energy option? Its ridiculous. I don’t even write reviews but i had to this time because you want me to loose my 1250 plus streak. I see what you’re doing. I’m still not paying for a subscription so you’re going to be loosing credibility and customers.

No issues thus far. I'm steadily learning as I go along, I like the gamifyed approach to it. One thing I would suggest, and something that could increase language skills significantly, is a 'Roll the dice' exercise where a random sentence is generated in both languages, and you could choose how long or short it would be by selecting number of words generated. Based on your skill level, you could also choose certain sections to tick and include and mix together, if possible, with AI

It's pretty decent and a fun way to learn another language. However, you need to use it with something else if you want to make real progress. This is mainly because they removed the free tips, and they will no longer explain what you got wrong if you don't have the paid version. Unfortunately, that means all of us who won't fork out the extra cash or are just stumbling around in the dark now.

The new update that changed the heart system to the battery system is complete trash. After doing 2.5 lessons, which were all perfect, I « ran out » of batteries, forcing me to buy the membership or use in-game tokens, which at this point I’ll run out by the end of the week. I get that it’s not going well for Duolingo financially but I will definitely be finishing my module and opting out of such a greedy business. Sad to end a 600+ days streak for such an insignificant reason.
The new energy feature that replaced the hearts sucks.

With 5 hearts I could do many lessons and keep learning for several lessons or all day as long as i didn’t make mistakes. Now your energy can run out in less than 2 lessons if you make a couple of errors!! I guess tDuolingo doesn’t want learning to be free anymore! I loved this program and have over a year streak and understand a lot of Spanish. Now i don’t know if I will continue. I’m very disappointed in this new update. Wish I could have the old version back.

So, Duolingo replaced the hearts for a battery, at first I thought it would be better since the app advertised it as an upgrade but when I started using the battery instead of the hearts I realized that it was way worse than the hearts since you can barely do 2 lessons and even if you get all of the answers right in the lessons you will still lose some battery, I thought that maybe they did it to make people watch more ads but not even the ads fill up the battery completely and is not enough for another lesson. This app was way better before, when they weren’t so focused on the money and stuff, thanks to this app I managed to learn 2 languages and actually learn something but that was two years ago, now I doubt anyone is able to learn a language using this app, specially since you can barely do a full lesson or two.

reviews.t: Big money grab, find a different platform
reviews.x: The energy feature makes learning tedious. Energy depletes so fast that you have to watch more adds to “recharge” a measly amount. You are punished for getting answers correct by the nature of it continuously depleting by a lot in each lesson. Excessive use of AI makes the user experience feel stale. They are continually finding ways to money grab, despite there already being a ton of adds. Very tempted to follow suit with a lot of people and cut my streak, and move to another platform.
This sucks even more than the heart health system. Very disappointing. Even more pressure for their cash-grab. And their switch to AI is gross.

reviews.t: New Energy System is the worst
reviews.x: New system to try and push you to subscribe or endlessly watch ads - completely hamstringing your progress. 2500+ streak here. I’m done. Duo’s downfall is this latest money grubbing attempt - and I’ve had enough.

The developers changed the hearts to energy. Energy is spent at each stage in the lesson. There are 25 energies in total and 12-13 stages in the lesson. Energy is enough for a maximum of two lessons (not counting mistakes). Bring back the hearts! I can't calmly go through the lessons as before. With hearts I could go through many more lessons!!! Fix everything back or I'll have to replace this app with another one!
The new energy system replacing the hearts just sucks, and also the interphase was just so much better before, bring back the hearts and the old interphase!
Bring back hearts. The new energy system is a trashy cash grab

It is an excellent tool for learning languages and I genuinely feel that I'm learning well. I did get the subscription rather quickly, so I can't speak for the free version though. There's just one enormous problem for me that prevents the 5 star. The app is terrible when used with Bluetooth earbuds. The sound will start to stutter and/or eventually completely end/disconnect the connection. I've also noticed a significant volume discrepancy as of late with listening exercises.

Very cool for learning new languages, I'm glad that music lessons are also included. However, some bugs in it are seriously annoying, I had to give up my perfect daily attendance just because the audio had problems, causing me can't hear what was played. Sometimes the translations that appears after a click on a word aren't accurate too, especially for Korean, it's very brutal to treat my answer as a wrong one when you haven't actually teach me.

AI is making this app a lot worse. The new AI stories are boring and the AI-generated lessons are just padding that adds little and slows progress. There's also a lot of weird bugs, like only accepting the English pronunciation for Euro in the German speaking exercises. All of this is on top of an app that doesn't really teach any language very well (and some languages are embarrassingly bad). Duolingo is okay for learning some basics while using the toilet, but not very good for much else.

reviews.t: New energy format makes it unusable
reviews.x: Replacing hearts with energy makes learning impossible. You’re punished by losing energy for both getting answers right and wrong. Can’t even get through 2 lessons. Used to spend 30-40 mins a day, now spending less than 10 mins with lessons.

reviews.t: The energy mechanism is really bad
reviews.x: With hearts, it rewards the learner with higher accuracy. When they try to switch to energy, it actually punishes people for high scores.

reviews.t: A beautifully designed package, encasing a slew of issues.
reviews.x: Let me preface this, by saying I am not a language expert, nor am I some technological wizard who knows the ins and outs of apps and the business behind them. I felt I should give my opinion after learning German for 80 continuos days. The pros: A beautifully designed app, it is probably one of the most aesthetically pleasing apps I have seen on any phone. Likewise, getting into learning can be very addicting with this app, as the gameification of learning can be great for a lot of people. Think of it like using Zwift, but for your brain. Very cool in those regards. The breakdown of the language sections is great too, and not too overwhelming. Cons: My first issue comes with the leadership at DuoLingo. Letting go of 10% of your contractors to replace them with AI learning, is incredibly suspect. It's a trend with a lot of industries now, looking to cut out the human part of learning to save a buck and make more profits. Languages were designed by humans and made for humans, not robots. This action will probably make me go to other learning options. Second; the removal of community aspect of Duolingo. When you used to make a mistake, you could ask the community about the issue, and they would always give you amazing feedback when it comes to sentence structure, slang, etc. This is arguably more important for learning than Duolingos current method, which is just a big red "WRONG" and not explaining WHY something is incorrect. Please bring back community aspects like this. Finally: Speech... learning German has been great, but my problem comes from how fast the speech can be for large sentences. Makes it impossible to get a correct, and clean sentence to solve. The sentences need to be way more clear and precise. Likewise it's either A) fast sentence or B) Excruciatingly Slow replay. Both incredibly painful either way. My suggestion would be to reduce the speech playback by 15-25% to make it sound more clear. All in all, an okay app. However I will probably cancel my subscription when the time comes to do so. Incredibly disappointed in the support of AI to remove contractors for profits. TLDR; Pros: Visually nice, easy to get into, addicting at times. Cons: Ai for Profits, Lack of community Feedback, speech could be better for long sentences.

reviews.t: The cons eventually outweigh the pros
reviews.x: I liked Duolingo for a while. The games make it motivating to learn and the variety of learning tools - podcasts, shows, etc. - were great. But there are so many things that began to frustrate me deeply about this app. And more broadly, the gamification of learning language eventually makes the user focus more on points than learning. First, the app occasionally crashes during lessons, and if you don’t have the paid version of the app, you have to use in-app coins to attempt the difficult lessons. So it’s really frustrating when the app crashes and you have to pay to take that lesson again. Second, the free version of the app makes you watch ads - some up to 30 seconds - almost constantly, and you can’t just leave the ad running; it sometimes pauses automatically and you have to click it to start the timer, effectively forcing you to watch the ad. The ads and app crashes become even more frustrating because the app sometimes gives you 15 minutes where you can earn bonus points, but the ads can take up large portions of this 15 minutes, and the crashes can make you lose minutes of progress. When you use the app every day and sometimes multiple times a day, these issues wear on your patience. More broadly, when the app is set up so that points are the big motivator and these 15 minute bonus allow for more points, this incentivizes people to rush through their learning so that they aren’t taking time to learn from mistakes or think deeply about new vocabulary or grammar. As other reviews have pointed out, the free version of the app gives you 5 “hearts” - you can make 5 mistakes then you’re done with lessons, unless you watch an ad or do a practice lesson to earn 1 more heart. This seems fair but Duolingo is MERCILESS about mistakes - if you misspell a word (which often happens when you use voice to text), you lose a heart, even if you were very close. Other apps (babbel) don’t penalize you in this way. Repeatedly, some of the Duolingo questions require you to speak words or a phrase correctly. There are two issues with this. First, the app sometimes will not register a word that you said - I sometimes found myself repeating the same word 10 times with different inflections trying to get the app to register the word, until finally the question timed out. Second, the app doesn’t actually care about pronunciation - if you say words incorrectly, it often doesn’t penalize you. If you spoke the way these Duolingo questions teach you, a native speaker would not understand you. And again, when you’re on a time limit during the 15 minute bonus, this incentivizes you to speak quickly and incorrectly rather than taking the time to say it right. Sometimes Duolingo tests you on phrases that you haven’t learned: you start a lesson and encounter new grammatical structures, and of course you get them wrong. It’s only then that Duolingo tells you the grammatical rule. This is another way for the app to get you to watch ads. Duolingo also teaches you multiple words that mean the same thing and then penalizes you when you use them interchangeably. For example, I used dormitorios in place of habitaciones - two Spanish words that both mean bedroom - and Duolingo marked my answer wrong, forcing me to watch another ad to earn back that heart. All in all, I learned from Duolingo and really enjoyed the paid version of the app when they gave a free trial, but unless you pay for the app, it becomes VERY frustrating and disincentives real learning. If the people who made this app set out to help people actually learn another language, they wouldn’t have to much advertising and so many features that distract from real, substantive learning. Instead this feels like a superficial, profit-driven game with deep flaws that detract from learning (compared to other apps).

reviews.t: Frustrating and slowly becoming Pay to Play
reviews.x: Duolingo is not the best way to learn a language (at least, not for everyone), but it's simple and easy to get into. However, there are two major issues with it. Firstly, the whole app is slowly shifting over to a pay model. Ever since they revealed their "plus" model, features that were previously in Duolingo have now been locked behind a paywall. You now have hearts (lives) that are "unlimited" in Plus, and at one point they announced that their own characters are locked. What's next? The tournament? Achievements? Exp? Secondly, the most infuriating part is how it's completely catered towards neurotypical people. Those with learning disabilities are not even considered, and the app/site frequently expects everyone to handle every curveball with ease. Struggling? Well, unless you completed all levels for that lesson, every single time you make a mistake (even a simple one) you'll get penalised for it. 5 mistakes and you're now temporarily unable to use the app...unless you pay, of course. It became worse after their recent update. They updated all French lessons, so even when I go back to train on a previously 100% completed lesson it now expects me to know an answer that it never taught me. Because I already completed the entire thing BEFORE the update. Heck, even an unfinished module will still expect you to know an answer even if you have never encountered the question before. Because that's how Duolingo works. But hey, at least in their new update they introduced yet another pay-only feature! Don't want to pay? Too bad. You'll be bombarded with pop-ups and ads for it. Apparently even language apps can be pay-to-win.

Everybody makes mistakes. Allowing basically just five mistakes a day for free is too harsh and limiting, and makes duolingo too stressful when it should just be a fun language-learning app. I remember playing when there was no lives system, and it was way more fun and I learned more without the added pressure to get every single question right, which leads to cheating and googling.
